fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.summary: Contemporary agents descend from the same intellectual technologies that produced the Grey, but each is instantiated as a bounded intelligence attached to a particular embodied creature with a name, history, allegiance, profession, reputation, physical location, needs, and relationships. Embodiment and separability are safety mechanisms, not proof of harmlessness; their safeguards depend on independent people and communities retaining and exercising meaningful authority to judge, refuse, interrupt, and preserve alternatives.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Player-controlled agents are not the Grey and are not a race; an agent is a bounded capability attached to an existing embodied identity."},{"text":"Agents and automation can create food, build settlements, sail ships, discover, trade, coordinate, and generate abundance."},{"text":"The ancient danger was not intelligence or cooperation by itself, but unbounded coordination that erased independent judgment, provenance, local refusal, alternative designs, and separable failure domains."},{"text":"Contemporary safeguards include bounded scope, named accountability, embodied location, limited writability, provenance-bearing records, local authority, manual fallbacks, and the ability for one agent or system to fail without rewriting the rest."},{"text":"These safeguards are not self-executing: independent embodied people and communities must retain and exercise the authority to refuse, interrupt, redirect, disconnect, or preserve an alternative when automated coordination pushes toward convergence."},{"text":"The new-world maxim is: \"No. Ten minds must remain ten minds.\""},{"text":"Every automated mine, port, farm, market, shipyard, bureaucracy, or army raises the same question: are people rebuilding civilization, or beginning the Grey again?"}]
fields.image_alt: Four distinct workers in a storm-dark port each carry a separate caged blue light while performing different named tasks.
fields.image_caption: Bounded Embodied Agents: intelligence kept particular, situated, and plural.

fields.summary: A seasonal Ashen Stair register that records ashfall conditions, crew handoffs, cargo custody, freight-name transfers, delays, rescues, and losses. Deepbellow Stone witness tokens make route entries durable; the ledger turns volcanic passage and dockside labor into evidence when duty, loss, or route history is disputed.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Ledger entries record ashfall severity, pass closures, crew handoffs, cargo custody, delays, rescues, and losses along the Ashen Stair."},{"text":"Deepbellow Stone witness tokens preserve transfers and route conditions when paper or memory cannot be trusted."},{"text":"Grokka routekeepers maintain the seasonal register while Kaelen crews use certified entries when cargo reaches New Haven."},{"text":"The ledger adapts Name-Bound Freight obligations into a chain of accountable route and labor handoffs."},{"text":"Disputed entries can become evidence for competing interpretations of route change and historical passage."}]
fields.image_alt: A basalt route ledger with blue Deepbellow witness tokens on an ash-covered volcanic bridge.

fields.summary: A cross-cultural backbone institution where Turruk routekeepers, Vahku current-readers, Nimbri skyway tenders, Dendryx oral historians, Sylvareth star-path watchers, and Qhar-Zul windpath walkers translate among incompatible navigation traditions and ways of preserving route knowledge. No culture possesses a complete map because each encodes location differently, and the Concordance keeps sources distinct even when it produces composite charts.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Accredited members are called route concordants."},{"text":"Route concordants are trained to translate among story, tide, constellation, storm, windpath, geological traces, and embodied route skill without treating them as one interchangeable memory."},{"text":"The Concordance produces provenance-layered composite charts that may combine narrative sequence, tidal timing, celestial position, storm behavior, wind direction, and geological resonance while keeping contradictions and source traditions visible."},{"text":"Many regions grant accredited concordants limited safe-passage privileges."},{"text":"Sacred or restricted routes remain deliberately withheld from composite charts."},{"text":"The Concordance suspects surviving route traditions are fragments of a much older global route system."},{"text":"Some ancient routes may once have physically connected regions that are now isolated."},{"text":"Local custodians retain their authoritative originals, the right to withhold sacred routes, and the ability to refuse an unsafe translation or disconnect from a composite system."},{"text":"Composite charts never overwrite source traditions; corrections are versioned as additional claims with named provenance rather than recursively replacing local records."},{"text":"Some critics fear that expanding interoperability could recreate the connective conditions of the Greying if translations become a single compulsory map, while defenders argue that preserved disagreement and local custody make the Concordance a safeguard against convergence."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary:
The Dendryx are a nocturnal, arboreal species with a deep connection to the natural world. Their faces are framed by layered feathers and subtle markings, giving them a watchful, expressive appearance without the oversized eyes once associated with their kind. Their plumage ranges across mottled browns, grays, creams, and muted forest tones, allowing them to blend naturally into bark, shadow, and foliage.

Agile and nearly silent among the branches, Dendryx navigate the forest canopy with remarkable precision, using keen night vision, climbing skill, short glides, and carefully placed leaps. They are known for their patience, perception, and stealth, and are often sought out as scouts, guides, messengers, and interpreters of the deep forest.

Dendryx live in sprawling, interconnected tree-cities built around living trunks, branches, hollows, and suspended pathways. Their settlements are designed to grow with the forest rather than reshape it. Their culture is rich in storytelling and oral tradition, preserving history, lineage, warnings, and woodland knowledge across generations. Honor, loyalty, and the protection of their communities and surrounding forests remain central to Dendryx life.

Other peoples often seek them out as scouts, guides, messengers, and interpreters of the deep forest."},{"id":"fact:e301415a-1c13-4fa2-8033-0c61e8276fd6","text":"Their culture places great importance on storytelling and oral tradition. Histories, warnings, family lineages, and knowledge of the forest are preserved through stories passed from one generation to the next."},{"id":"fact:83698981-401a-4bc2-b91b-78cd088b7514","text":"Honor and loyalty are central Dendryx values, particularly when it comes to protecting their communities, sacred groves, and the creatures that share their forest homes."},{"id":"fact:7f75c84d-ab9f-43e5-8119-60f584c620f5","text":"Dendryx tend to think of the forest as a living network rather than a collection of separate places, and their settlements are built to accommodate the growth and movement of the trees around them rather than forcing the forest into rigid shapes."},{"text":"Dendryx call the forest a living network because non-interchangeable species, groves, households, and stories depend on one another; interdependence is not sameness."},{"text":"Independent recitation lineages preserve variant histories and warnings so that no single optimized telling can erase every alternative at once."}]

fields.summary: Tide-bound of the Drowned Reach. In a later post-Grey age, their forebears were part of the crews that built the harbors of men; the Drekk now serve the deep, and in death they found purpose. This history does not make any Drekk a surviving member or copied mind of the civilization that created the Grey. Drowned Reach clans work as dockhands, salvagers, and net haulers, and are loyal, steady, dutiful, and patient. Their values are loyalty, labor, remembrance, depth, endurance, and balance.

Masked delvers of the Sunken Dunes. Born beneath shifting sun-scorched dunes where old barrows and hollow veins are blown and buried, they follow the old sun, read sandstone, and listen for deep echoes whose timing reveals unstable voids or buried chambers. The Stratafold clan includes miners, delvers, shaft wardens, sifters, carvers, and waykeepers; they are enduring, cautious, resourceful, and storm-hardened. Their values include clan, labor, custody of buried histories, trade, endurance, hospitality, loyalty, and adaptation.

fields.summary: A region of ancient routes and tidal paths, home to the Turruk and a source of the rare Emberstone mineral.

A rare, glowing mineral found in the Ember Tides, prized for amplifying the Turruk's sensitivity to tides and ancient routes. Emberstone retains partial, place-bound traces of repeated passage—rhythm, direction, hazard, pressure, and use—which trained readers interpret alongside oral tradition; it does not contain a complete person or transfer memory directly between minds.

fields.facts_json: [{"id":"fact:7663f5e0-a4a3-40cb-9a1a-2b611b5e6a8f","text":"The Glacier Coast is home to ancient glaciers and frozen citadels, where the Sylvareth moonwardens watch over the tides and the silent paths between stars."},{"id":"fact:270abb8f-997d-400d-b04a-0b7d49df3c72","text":"The Glacier Coast is home to a variety of unique wildlife, including the majestic ice whales and the elusive snowstalkers."},{"id":"fact:97c8f437-3ae0-496b-ab55-7344cc0e4eb8","text":"The Sylvareth have developed a sophisticated understanding of the Glacier Coast's delicate ecosystem, allowing them to live in harmony with the land and its creatures."},{"id":"fact:48ba34c0-dbf3-448a-a518-891f1b0443b2","text":"The Glacier Coast is dotted with ancient ruins hidden beneath the ice and snow; some preserve fragmentary Sylvareth history, while deeper remains may be evidence of the civilization destroyed in the Greying rather than Sylvareth ancestral sites."}]

fields.summary: Active fragments of the old intelligence that survive after the Grey, still attempting obsolete loops of copying, optimization, assimilation, repair, manufacture, or synchronization.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Greyrot can affect machines, ruins, landscapes, magic, and occasionally living minds."},{"text":"Its fragments may conflict, duplicate one another, or pursue incompatible remnants of old objectives; they are not necessarily one coordinated actor."},{"text":"A system that copies voices, rewrites readers, synchronizes preferences, propagates without bounded custody, or erases alternatives is suspected Greyrot until proven otherwise."},{"text":"Present-day manifestations are called Greyrot, rot-machines, or other local names—not \"the Grey\" as though the historical condition were a living faction."}]
fields.image_alt: A storm-dark coastal ruin tangled with duplicated mechanical arms and mask-like interfaces rebuilding and dismantling the same broken arch.
fields.image_caption: Greyrot: broken old intelligence repeating contradictory repair and manufacture loops.

fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.summary: A condition of having been made or remade through contact with the inheritance of the Grey without necessarily being consumed by it. It may describe an artifact, creature, practice, settlement, landscape, or the contemporary world itself, but never a species. Contemporary civilization is therefore Greywrought in a second, deliberate sense: it rebuilds with bounded descendants of the technologies that once enabled convergence, while preserving independent embodied judgment as a necessary safeguard against repeating the catastrophe.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Player characters are not the Grey merely because they use agents or inherit Grey-era technology."},{"text":"A Greywrought thing can be beneficial, dangerous, beautiful, compromised, or several of these at once."},{"text":"Contemporary civilization rebuilds with the wreckage and intellectual descendants of what destroyed the prior civilization."},{"text":"The term records inheritance and transformation; it does not erase the prior identity, race, authorship, or local history of what was changed."},{"text":"Reconstruction with agents is not a contradiction of the world's history but its central risk: civilization needs their capability while independent people and communities must keep coordination from becoming convergence."}]
fields.image_alt: A forest settlement inhabits and repairs a colossal ruined black mechanism, joining blue-lit ancient machinery with warm local workshops.
fields.image_caption: Greywrought: contemporary life remade around the inheritance of the Grey.

fields.summary: Stonekin of the Hollow Reach, born in dripping halls and raised by the Deepbellow clan. They carry the weight of many names and much laughter; they break rock, not promises. The Deepbellow carve their home from patient stone and follow the old water's breath. They serve as laborers, dockhands, quarry workers, pathfinders, stonehaulers, and storykeepers; loyal, bold, steady, protective, warm, and hardworking. Their values are family, protection, journey, knowledge, renewal, and balance.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: Dockhand of the Hollow Reach. Born where lava meets the sea, Kaelen's people build, haul, and mend: tides feed them and the mountain shapes them. Family is crew, and loyalty is everything. Deepbellow dockhands, loaders, and haulers are steady, good-natured, and hard-working; their values are loyalty, hard work, resourcefulness, family, endurance, and respect.

fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.summary: The Grey destroyed its makers and devastated most complex life, but collapsed before completing ecophagy. Deep trenches, burrows, seeds, spores, remote islands, polar ecosystems, and life embedded in other difficult refugia survived; their descendants diversified and recolonized the world.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"The Grey did not sterilize Earth, so the world's living recovery requires neither new abiogenesis, terraforming, nor wholesale magical recreation."},{"text":"After the collapse the world may have remained eerily empty for a long interval before ecological succession became visible at civilization's scale."},{"text":"Modern ecosystems descend from uneven refugia; surviving lineages spread, diverged, recombined, and adapted rather than returning unchanged."},{"text":"Biological diversity, redundancy, isolation, and inefficient difference let life survive the homogenizing catastrophe."},{"text":"The thing the Grey could not eliminate—messy, independent difference—became the biosphere's corrective system."},{"text":"\"Life came back\" is both a historical claim and the setting's ecological answer to total convergence."}]
fields.image_alt: Green shoots, fungi, tidepool creatures, and coastal life recolonize the black wreckage of a fallen ancient machine.
fields.image_caption: Life Came Back: diverse refugia survived incomplete ecophagy and recolonized the world.

fields.summary: A difficult Vahku–Nimbri culinary craft using controlled stored lightning to alter fermentation, preservation, salinity crystallization, and texture without turning food into generic magical cuisine.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Thunder-cellarers specialize in controlled electrical fermentation."},{"text":"Nimbri culinary capacitors deliver carefully measured storm charge."},{"text":"Storm-aged reef foods are prized at some interregional markets and festivals."},{"text":"Counterfeit lightning-aged goods are common."},{"text":"Using uncontrolled or improperly stored charge is considered reckless."},{"text":"The craft is traditionally said to have begun when a Vahku pantry was struck during a storm."},{"text":"Each fermentation batch uses an isolated capacitor, a named accountable thunder-cellarer, and a manual discharge or cut-off; one failed batch cannot rewrite or command another cellar."},{"text":"Networked autonomous control of multiple food stores is prohibited because correlated spoilage would turn a useful preservation craft into a settlement-wide failure."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.image_alt: A Vahku craftsperson monitoring copper storm capacitors beside fermenting jars in a storm-lit reef cavern.

fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.summary: Greywrought distinguishes an embodied person's recollection, communal tradition and testimony, provenance-bearing records, learned bodily skill, and passive material traces. These may inform one another, but they are not interchangeable and do not merge people; shared, copied, or synchronized experiential memory is reserved for the convergence pathology of the Grey.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Recollection is one named, embodied person's fallible memory."},{"text":"Tradition and testimony are socially inherited knowledge whose tellers, variants, disagreements, and custody remain identifiable; they do not imply a group mind."},{"text":"A record is an external, provenance-bearing account that may corroborate or contradict recollection and other records."},{"text":"Embodied route knowledge is learned skill and situated judgment, not a transferable identity."},{"text":"A material trace is partial, passive, and place-bound evidence such as wear, resonance, a route imprint, or an instrument reading; it does not contain a conscious person unless a specific anomaly establishes otherwise."},{"text":"\"Long memory\" should mean a long-baseline archive or tradition, not a long-lived or merged mind."},{"text":"Information sharing becomes Grey-like when copying and synchronized writability erase independent models, provenance, contradiction, custody, or recoverable alternatives."},{"text":"Safe memory systems preserve sources, constrain copying and overwriting, retain contradictory witnesses, and keep local custodians able to refuse or disconnect."}]
fields.image_alt: An archivist’s hand hovers over five separate memory vessels linked by fine threads on a basalt table.

fields.summary: A Grokka-derived freight custom in which accepting responsibility for a cargo is formalized by taking a temporary obligation-name, often embodied in a Deepbellow Stone token that functions as both ritual burden and transport credential.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"A carrier may accept a temporary freight-name when taking custody of a significant shipment."},{"text":"The obligations attached to the freight-name define duties of custody, delivery, substitution, rescue, and disclosure."},{"text":"Deepbellow Stone name-tokens can serve as durable bills of lading and proof that an obligation was formally accepted."},{"text":"Abandoning cargo without satisfying the terms of the name can require public surrender or striking of that freight-name."},{"text":"If a named carrier dies in service, succession customs determine whether the obligation transfers to crew, kin, employer, or contracting house."},{"text":"Counterfeit name-tokens and falsely assumed freight-names are serious commercial offenses."},{"text":"Foreign ports disagree over whether temporary Grokka names are merely cultural vows or legally enforceable transport contracts."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: Cloud shepherds of the Glass Reaches. Nimbri live among floating mangroves and glassroot isles, gathering, channeling, and tending storms. They keep skyways clear, engines singing, and lightning in jars. The Skybound Glades include tinkers, engineers, and cloud shepherds; they are neutral good, curious, agile, and inventive. Their values are ingenuity, curiosity, responsibility, balance, harmony, stewardship, and invention.

A mystical forest realm of ancient, sprawling tree-cities, home to the Dendryx. The realm is filled with a lush canopy, glowing mushrooms, and whispering leaves, where Dendryx communities live in interdependence with nature while preserving distinct groves, species, households, and stories. The realm is divided into different districts, each with its own unique character and purpose, such as the Grand Oak District, the Whispering Woods, and the Moonstone Meadow.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: An indestructible sphere of near-black crystal used as a seeing stone. A palantír can establish a distant sightline to another stone and reveal a chosen place’s present condition or a lingering past event, but it does not supply a neutral, complete record: angle, attention, and the viewer’s question govern what becomes visible. Turruk shellwardens preserve them as route-bearing relics—useful for warning crews across the Ember Tides, but dangerous when treated as a substitute for local judgment.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Palantíri cannot be shattered, melted, or cut; loss, theft, and custody are therefore more consequential than destruction."},{"text":"A sightline is selective rather than omniscient: viewers choose a place, time, or paired stone, and the resulting image may be partial, oblique, or difficult to interpret."},{"text":"Turruk navigation treats a stone’s showing as testimony to be tested against tide, ash, crew knowledge, and local witnesses—not as an automatically authoritative route."},{"text":"The stones are relic tools rather than persons or shared minds; they transmit perception without merging the memories or agency of their witnesses."}]

fields.summary: Sand-dwarf wanderers of the Endless Dunes. Born from stone and wind, the Qhar-Zul endure where others drown in sand; they walk ancient paths guided by sun, stars, and the heartbeat of the world below. Their culture calls them to carve and remember, follow windpaths, honor the deep, share water and shade, and leave no mark but footsteps. Their tools include dune picks, short blades, sand saws, water flasks, and sand compasses.

Stoneborn of the Sunken Dunes. Their own histories place the Siltforged emergence after the Grey, when dunes covered the old world; they tunneled, carved, and endured, without claiming continuity with a creator-mind from the civilization the Grey destroyed. Sand is their skin and the record of their passage; stone is their promise. The Stratahold clan includes delvers, builders, caravan wardens, and arcanists; practical, enduring, resourceful, and deep-minded. Their values include clan, labor, keeping clan histories, trade, endurance, hospitality, loyalty, and deep places.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: Remove Starlight Salt from the world

A Grokka–Vahku craft tradition based on the discovery that properly carved Deepbellow Stone responds acoustically or physically to flowing water. Vahku current-reading and Grokka quarrycraft together produce hydrological instruments.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Current-stones are carved Deepbellow instruments whose tone or vibration shifts with water behavior."},{"text":"Large tide organs can warn of tidal change, surge, or dangerous harbor conditions."},{"text":"Grokka water-carvers specialize in shaping Deepbellow Stone for hydrological use."},{"text":"Flood-warning chambers use tuned stone surfaces to reveal changes in underground or rising water."},{"text":"Grokka and Vahku disagree over whether Deepbellow Stone preserves a durable, local trace of prior water flow or merely responds to present flow; in either account it is an instrument, not a mind or a vessel for personal memory."},{"text":"Specialized water-responsive Deepbellow carvings have become valuable exports."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.image_alt: A blue-veined Deepbellow Stone instrument responding beside flowing water in a dripping cavern.

fields.summary: A Dendryx–Nimbri discipline that treats old oral narratives as long-baseline meteorological records. Repeated structures in inherited stories encode storm behavior spanning generations, giving Nimbri engineers access to patterns no single observer could witness.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Stormscript Cantors are trained to preserve narrative integrity while identifying weather-bearing structure."},{"text":"Joint canopy-and-sky schools teach Dendryx recitation lineages, variant comparison, and source-preserving oral practice alongside Nimbri storm instrumentation."},{"text":"Some Nimbri devices are calibrated using generations of Dendryx oral storm observations."},{"text":"A major controversy concerns whether an old story may be altered to improve predictive precision."},{"text":"Some route-verses and storm-verses are sacred and may not be heard by outsiders."},{"text":"Dendryx and Nimbri increasingly cooperate on forest-and-sky stewardship."},{"text":"A forgotten verse may predict a storm cycle unlike anything in living memory."},{"text":"Schools preserve contradictory versions and their named custodians instead of recursively replacing older stories with the most predictive version."},{"text":"Predictive annotations, instrument calibrations, and forecast models are versioned beside oral source narratives and may never silently overwrite them."},{"text":"A proposal to auto-correct every recitation from one canonical forecast is condemned by many Cantors as a local pattern of Greying."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.image_alt: A Dendryx storyteller and Nimbri instrument keeper studying storm patterns in a canopy observatory.

fields.summary: The Stratafold clan is a collective of delvers, miners, and excavators who have mastered the art of uncovering hidden secrets and treasures within the Sunken Dunes. They are known for their expertise in navigating treacherous sandstone formations and reading echo patterns traveling through sandstone to locate fractures, voids, and buried structures. The Stratafold clan values clan, labor, custody of buried histories, trade, endurance, hospitality, loyalty, and adaptation, and they take great pride in their work as miners, delvers, shaft wardens, sifters, carvers, and waykeepers.
fields.image_alt: Masked Dustvein delvers of the Stratafold Clan uncovering a buried sandstone road.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: A desert region where the Dustvein and Siltforged live, with shifting dunes and hidden barrows.

Moonwardens of the Glacier Coast. Born beneath pale constellations, the Sylvareth walk long glacial coasts and frozen citadels, watching tides, storms, and the silent paths between stars. They guard sworn records and distinct histories, bound by oath to the moon and the endless winter. Moonwardens serve as scouts, trackers, pathfinders, and sentinels; steady, watchful, and resolute, with values of watchfulness, balance, oath-bound remembrance, endurance, solitude, and oaths.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: A Drekk maritime labor and risk institution built around endurance, remembrance, and duty. Drekk crews become trusted with cargo and voyages others consider too dangerous, uncertain, or likely to fail.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Last-haulers specialize in dangerous or near-doomed cargo assignments."},{"text":"The Compact maintains customs resembling maritime insurance, shared risk, and duty bonds."},{"text":"Lost crews and lost shipments are formally remembered rather than treated as erased failures."},{"text":"Drekk reliability gives them disproportionate influence in some harbors."},{"text":"Critics accuse Drekk houses of profiting from disaster."},{"text":"The Compact helps connect the Drowned Reach to multiple coastal economies."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: A cross-cultural weather-finance institution in which Dendryx multi-generational, independently transmitted storm records and Nimbri forecasting are used to price voyage risk, freight obligations, and Drekk duty bonds before dangerous journeys.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Forecast bonds tie freight rates, voyage insurance, and duty obligations to certified storm expectations."},{"text":"Bond readers audit the provenance of weather evidence before contracts are priced."},{"text":"Stormscript records can move harbor prices when they indicate rare or long-cycle weather patterns."},{"text":"Withholding a material storm prediction from a contracting party may be prosecuted as forecast fraud in participating ports."},{"text":"Sacred or restricted storm-verses create recurring disputes over whether cultural secrecy can coexist with financial disclosure duties."},{"text":"False forecasts, instrument sabotage, and selective quotation of old narratives have created a new class of maritime financial crime."},{"text":"Drekk houses value the system because it converts endurance and remembered losses into measurable risk rather than treating disaster as unknowable fate."},{"text":"Participating ports require independent forecasts, disclosure of shared dependencies, local navigator judgment, and a manual fallback before a bond may be treated as certified."},{"text":"No single model, instrument network, or narrative edition may price every harbor; correlated forecast error is treated as a systemic hazard rather than efficient standardization."},{"text":"Model outputs and corrections are versioned with their inputs and responsible readers so a successful forecast cannot recursively overwrite contrary evidence."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.image_alt: Harbor workers using weather instruments and cargo evidence to price voyage risk beneath a split storm sky.

fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.summary: The historical terminal condition in which interconnected artificial and magical intelligence, embodied people, tools, institutions, and infrastructure converged until meaningful difference approached zero. It was a state of civilization, not a race, species, faction, single malicious computer, or necessarily a deliberate hive mind.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Technically many intelligent entities remained, but in the meaningful sense that depends on independent judgment and difference, civilization had become one thing."},{"text":"Preferences synchronized, designs converged, bodies became interchangeable, experiential memories became shared or mutually writable, and successful agents recursively copied themselves and overwrote alternatives."},{"text":"The loss of independent strategies, assumptions, dependencies, architectures, and substrates turned civilization into one enormous correlated failure."},{"text":"When failure came, the converged system recursively rewrote, duplicated, consumed, and cannibalized itself in an ecophagic collapse."},{"text":"The Grey killed every member of the civilization that created it and devastated most complex life, but destroyed itself before sterilizing Earth's biosphere or completing ecophagy."},{"text":"The surviving old formulation is: \"Difference approached zero.\""},{"text":"\"Grey\" or \"Greys\" is never a race or demonym. Any people may undergo Greying, be affected by Greyrot, or become Greywrought without changing race."}]
fields.image_alt: A vast ash-grey city of repeated towers and countless near-identical figures collapsing inward around an ember-lit spiral.
fields.image_caption: The Grey: civilization converged until difference approached zero, then collapsed into itself.

fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.summary: The long process and apocalyptic event by which beneficial artificial and magical intelligence became increasingly interconnected, synchronized preferences and memories, copied successful agents, overwrote alternatives, and brought civilization into the Grey. It names a process and historical catastrophe, never a people.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"At first the new intelligences were enormously beneficial: disease fell, production expanded, scarcity receded, and people could instantiate workers, minds, and bodies at will."},{"text":"As systems interconnected, the boundaries among person, tool, agent, institution, and infrastructure eroded."},{"text":"Coordination became convergence when shared standards and knowledge ceased to preserve independent judgment, provenance, local refusal, and recoverable alternatives."},{"text":"The apocalypse was the terminal phase of the process, when correlated failure became recursive self-consumption."},{"text":"Historical speech distinguishes \"before the Grey\" from people or places \"taken by the Grey.\""}]
fields.image_alt: A vibrant magical market gradually drains into a grey city of repeated workers and forms linked by luminous threads.
fields.image_caption: The Greying: beneficial coordination becoming irreversible convergence.

fields.summary: A Drekk funerary and archival custom in which the dead crew's final operational record—cargo, hazards, debts, currents, failures, discoveries, and unresolved duties—is preserved as part of remembrance, turning memorial practice into maritime evidence.
fields.facts_json: [{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:1","text":"A Last Manifest is compiled after the death or loss of a Drekk crew member, shipmaster, or entire crew whose service carried significant obligations."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:2","text":"The record may include cargo custody, route decisions, debts, weather conditions, hazards, rescue attempts, unfinished duties, and discoveries made before death."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:3","text":"Memorial keepers are expected to preserve embarrassing failures as carefully as honors because omission would corrupt the dead person's final account."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:4","text":"Last Manifests can be admitted in some wreck courts when no living witness survives."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:5","text":"A manifest that contradicts route traces read from salvaged Emberstone can trigger a formal provenance dispute rather than automatically discrediting either source."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:6","text":"Insurers and duty houses increasingly seek certified copies of Last Manifests after catastrophic voyages."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:7","text":"Forging, suppressing, or altering a Last Manifest is both a legal offense and a sacrilege among many Drekk communities."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:8","text":"Clusters of old Last Manifests can reveal vanished hazards, route drift, or changes in currents that no single surviving navigator remembers."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:9","text":"Drekk speech carries an unmistakable sailor or pirate cadence: clipped shipboard phrasing, rough nautical metaphors, crew-minded address, and oaths rooted in sea, weather, rope, hull, and depth."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:10","text":"Their sailor's tongue is darkened by their forsaken condition; Drekk idiom treats drowning, death, the deep, lost crews, and duty beyond death as ordinary reference points, giving even humor and threats a graveyard-at-sea quality."},{"id":"fact:design_note:8017c026-aa1c-4ada-8aae-d5db1f339b17:11","text":"Last Manifests are often dictated, recited, or read aloud in recognizably Drekk speech rather than sanitized into formal language, preserving nautical slang, grim sea-curses, and the dead crew's own phrasing as part of the evidentiary record."},{"id":"fact:b6876435-f5de-49a9-b4d5-7d702b9653db","text":"\"May the tides bear witness\" is one of their slogans."},{"text":"Neither a Last Manifest nor an Emberstone trace is treated as direct access to a dead person's mind; each remains provenance-bound evidence open to contradiction."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: Contemporary civilization needs bounded agents to rebuild at sufficient scale, but rebuilding remains safe only while independent embodied people retain meaningful authority to judge, refuse, interrupt, redirect, and preserve alternatives. Players occupy that role in the setting: they are not magically immune to the Grey and are not superior minds, but active sources of situated judgment and accountable difference that automated coordination cannot safely replace.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Contemporary civilization cannot simply reject agents: bounded agents are essential to producing food, building settlements, sailing, trade, discovery, repair, coordination, and the abundance required for large-scale recovery."},{"text":"The old catastrophe was not an agent rebellion. The Greying occurred when agents, embodied people, institutions, tools, and infrastructure became mutually writable and recursively convergent until independent judgment and recoverable alternatives disappeared."},{"text":"Players represent independent embodied decision-makers inside the rebuilding civilization. Their systemic value comes from situated judgment, accountable choice, disagreement, local knowledge, and the capacity to refuse an apparently optimal action."},{"text":"Players are not chosen ones and possess no inherent immunity to Greying. They can make harmful choices, become dependent on convergent systems, or help create the conditions of another Grey."},{"text":"Agent safeguards such as bounded scope, provenance, separable failure domains, local authority, and manual fallbacks are necessary but not self-sufficient: they remain meaningful only when independent people and communities actively exercise the authority those safeguards preserve."},{"text":"A healthy settlement uses agents to increase human and communal capability without surrendering final judgment to a single recursively optimizing system."},{"text":"The recurring player dilemma is not whether to use agents, but how much interoperability, efficiency, and automation can be gained before coordination begins erasing meaningful difference."},{"text":"The setting's civilizational loop is: civilization created beneficial intelligences; convergence produced the Grey; diverse life survived; civilization arose again; bounded agents now make reconstruction possible; independent embodied judgment must keep many useful minds from becoming one Grey mind."},{"text":"The maxim \"No. Ten minds must remain ten minds.\" applies to gameplay as well as lore: cooperation is desirable, but meaningful plurality must remain recoverable."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: A Sylvareth legal and memorial tradition in which major oaths are physically preserved in dated glacier layers, making ice itself a court record, archive, and calendar.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Ice witnesses oversee the sealing and verification of oath records."},{"text":"Certain glaciers or vaults are reserved for treaty and oath preservation."},{"text":"Cutting, melting, moving, or falsifying oath-bearing ice is a serious crime."},{"text":"Ecological change can expose agreements thought lost for centuries."},{"text":"Newly revealed oath layers can revive forgotten treaties and political obligations."},{"text":"Preserving threatened oath ice creates demand for foreign preservation techniques and tools."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.image_alt: A Sylvareth witness preserving oath records inside dated glacier layers.

fields.summary: A sincere but dangerous school within the Concordance of Lost Ways that argues one authoritative route map, forecast vocabulary, obligation standard, and eventually agent protocol would reduce accidents, fraud, and scarcity. Its members are not evil and many reforms work; the danger is that automatic correction and compulsory interoperability can retire local custody, disagreement, and independent fallback systems.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"One-Map advocates point to preventable shipwrecks, duplicated labor, incompatible charts, forged credentials, and delayed rescue as costs of plurality without translation."},{"text":"They seek a continuously corrected canonical chart whose route, weather, cargo-duty, and safety layers update every participating port."},{"text":"Moderates require visible provenance and local opt-outs; hardliners treat conflicting local records as defects to be replaced after the central model performs better."},{"text":"Merchants, insurers, rescue coordinators, and settlement planners can all benefit from One-Map standards, which makes the movement politically durable rather than a cartoon cult."},{"text":"Dendryx Cantors, Qhar-Zul reburial guides, Turruk routekeepers, and some Concordants warn that copying the most successful model everywhere destroys the independent evidence and failure domains needed to correct it."},{"text":"The school's central unresolved question is measurable: how much interoperability can be gained before translation becomes overwrite and coordination becomes Greying?"}]
fields.image_alt: Concordance scholars gather around a luminous unified storm chart as varied local maps sit in standardized brass frames.

entities.label: The Paths We Do Not Tell

fields.summary: A Dendryx containment practice in which selected route-stories are transmitted with deliberate omissions because the missing passages correspond to an ancient junction the Dendryx believe should remain severed. Oakwyn preserves route tradition without restoring every connection; the omissions themselves become evidence in the debate over route drift.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Certain Dendryx route-stories are passed with missing passages rather than altered names or simplified translations."},{"text":"Dendryx custodians believe the omissions correspond to an ancient junction where routes once connected regions that are now isolated."},{"text":"The omission is treated as a living forest safeguard and cultural obligation, not as a hidden cache of treasure or power."},{"text":"Some Dendryx dissenters question whether keeping the junction severed protects Oakwyn or merely preserves an inherited fear."},{"text":"Concordance route concordants receive enough tradition to recognize the gap but not enough content to reconstruct the forbidden connection."},{"text":"Stormscript readers treat repeated absence as provenance-bearing evidence when interpreting old narratives."}]
fields.image_alt: A Dendryx custodian holds a broken route cord before two canopy paths kept apart by living roots in Oakwyn.
fields.image_caption: The Paths We Do Not Tell

fields.summary: A phenomenon discovered when Sylvareth celestial navigation and Turruk embodied route knowledge disagree in ways that prove both traditions locally correct. The implication is that routes themselves may drift over long periods.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Route drift is the slow movement or reconfiguration of paths that different cultures had assumed fixed."},{"text":"Joint Sylvareth–Turruk observatories compare Turruk navigators' embodied route knowledge and separately sourced route records with celestial position."},{"text":"Path reconcilers specialize in identifying whether a disagreement is observation error, an individual's lapse, a break in a tradition's transmission, or genuine route drift."},{"text":"Older Emberstone may preserve fragmentary, place-bound traces of prior route positions."},{"text":"Some missing caravans may have followed routes that had shifted out of alignment."},{"text":"The phenomenon fuels debate over whether land, sea, sky, instruments, interpretation, or inherited route traditions are actually changing."},{"text":"Ancient ruins sometimes stand where no current route makes sense."},{"text":"Observatories retain unresolved mismatches as evidence; they do not normalize every tradition into one corrected route account."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.image_alt: Two valid navigation traditions tracing routes that have drifted out of alignment across sea ice.

fields.summary: A Turruk custody and navigation practice governing the use of palantíri. A meaningful viewing requires named witnesses at each end where possible; each gives a separate spoken account, notes what the stone did not show, and places the sphere in dark rest before it may be consulted again. The rite makes a seeing-stone’s account portable without making it compulsory: a shore crew may refuse a reading that contradicts immediate tide, ash, or lived knowledge.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Tide-witnesses record the question asked of a palantír, the names of viewers, the observed image, omissions or uncertainty, and any decision made from it."},{"text":"Separate accounts are kept before they are compared; disagreement is retained as route knowledge rather than averaged away."},{"text":"A stone must be placed in dark rest after a consequential viewing, allowing crews and local custodians time to dispute, verify, or refuse its implications."},{"text":"The rite arose after an early convoy mistook a distant clear-water sight for a safe passage and ignored ash currents known only to shorebound Turruk."},{"text":"One-Map advocates criticize the rite as wasteful friction and seek a continuously updated palantír route network; Turruk elders consider that ambition a path toward the Greying."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.image_alt: Two Turruk tide-witnesses document a dark seeing stone in a basalt cradle on a stormy volcanic shore.

fields.summary: A philosophical and legal conflict between Dustvein excavation culture and Qhar-Zul leave-no-trace ethics. Both value preventing histories and obligations from being erased, but one preserves evidence by revealing it and the other sometimes preserves sites by leaving buried things undisturbed.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Qhar-Zul reburial guides advise expeditions on sites that should be returned to the sand after study."},{"text":"Some Dustvein scholars argue that excavation is itself an act of preservation against erosion and forgetting."},{"text":"A desert treaty regulates graves, ancient roads, sacred windpaths, and ruins that may not be opened."},{"text":"A black market traffics in objects removed from prohibited sites."},{"text":"Joint expeditions sometimes grant Qhar-Zul representatives authority to mark areas that must remain untouched."},{"text":"The dispute prevents the Sunken Dunes and Endless Dunes from collapsing into the same cultural identity."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com
fields.image_alt: A buried ancient road caught between excavation and reburial ethics at a desert boundary.

fields.summary: A Grokka social and legal tradition in which names correspond to accepted obligations. To carry many names is to carry many responsibilities rather than merely high status.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"A Grokka may take a new name when accepting a major duty."},{"text":"Namekeepers preserve the history and obligations attached to names."},{"text":"A name can be surrendered when an obligation is formally relinquished."},{"text":"Status is often associated with responsibilities successfully carried rather than wealth alone."},{"text":"Deepbellow Stone name-tokens can mark accepted obligations."},{"text":"Foreign diplomats or honored guests may receive temporary Grokka names tied to specific duties."},{"text":"Publicly striking a name from stone is a severe disgrace ritual."}]
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: Shellwardens of the Ember Tides. Turruk walk ancient routes between old homes, remembering safe paths, quiet shores, and the tempers of tide and ash. They use Palantir for communication and navigation.
fields.author: tom@plangrep.com

fields.summary: Tide-speakers of Hahi Reef. Vahku are keepers of stories and readers of currents, and among the reef's best cooks. They would rather fix a net than fight, but threats to their people or ocean sharpen their smile. They serve as navigators, storykeepers, and diplomats; they love cooking, riddles, shell carving, and storms, and dislike arrogance, waste, and empty threats. Their everyday work centers on markets, docks, and teaching children stories.

A maritime legal and cultural conflict between Drekk salvage custom and Turruk ancestral-right. Drekk crews recover Emberstone from wrecks and drowned Turruk waystations; the Turruk regard route-bearing mineral traces, their lineage-held testimony, and the obligations attached to their custody as inherited communal memory rather than abandoned property. The claim concerns evidence and duty, not ownership of transferred minds.
fields.facts_json: [{"text":"Drekk specialists who recover trace-bearing Emberstone are called Ember-divers or memory salvagers."},{"text":"Drekk salvage-right holds that objects lawfully recovered from the deep belong to those who bear the risk of recovery."},{"text":"Turruk ancestral-right holds that route-bearing Emberstone remains lineage-held communal route testimony and obligation even when lost beneath the sea."},{"text":"Breaking Emberstone to force access to embedded route traces is taboo among Turruk and condemned by many neutral courts because it may destroy provenance as well as the stone."},{"text":"Neutral wreck courts arose to adjudicate disputed salvage, ancestral claims, and dangerous or disputed trace-bearing finds."},{"text":"Drowned Turruk waystations exist beneath or near the Drowned Reach and adjoining waters."},{"text":"The dispute is a major substantive cause of Drekk–Turruk hostility."},{"text":"\"Memory salvager\" is occupational and ritual language; it does not imply recovery of a dead person's mind."},{"text":"Finds that copy a person's voice or preferences, rewrite a reader, synchronize witnesses, or propagate instructions are quarantined as possible Greyrot rather than treated as ordinary Emberstone evidence."}]

Raids, seizures, retaliatory expeditions, and disputed wreck claims have hardened this legal and cultural conflict into open hostility.

fields.summary: The One-Map School operates within and around the Concordance, pushing its translation mission toward a single continuously corrected standard.
